comparisons.D17: Use probability measures on the torus, or their unit-cell representatives, and couplings with first marginal P and second marginal Q. The cost is squared quotient distance induced by the Euclidean norm on R^d, not raw representative distance or the default coordinatewise sup norm. Integrate once over the torus/unit cell, not over the entire periodic infinite measure on R^d. Define the dual with P-integrable phi and Q-integrable psi and the inequality at EVERY pair x,y; L1 almost-everywhere equivalence classes alone do not specify those pointwise values. Compactness bounds the cost, but proving primal finiteness, dual feasibility and equality of infimum and supremum remains transport mathematics; neither Bochner integration nor a totalized real sInf/sSup proves it. Preserve the distinction from the Euclidean display using L1(Omega). The display is W2 squared.

comparisons.D10: In the Euclidean one-sample setting, define phi0(x)=norm(x)^2-2*varphi0(x) and psi0(y)=norm(y)^2-2*varphi0_star(y), with conjugation as the preceding source supremum over Omega. The factor two and source/target order are essential. The map is gradient varphi0 where differentiable; generic gradient/ConvexOn does not produce a Brenier optimizer. These corrections must be shown integrable and dual-optimal. Additive constants in the Brenier potential change the two corrections oppositely; the source supplies bounded representatives in this section, not a universally mean-zero convention.
comparisons.D19: The same algebraic formulas are applied to the convex lifted potential on R^d in the torus two-sample setting. The lift varphi0 itself is not periodic; norm(x)^2/2-varphi0(x) is periodic, and this is what lets the corrected potential descend to the torus. The transported map is interpreted modulo Z^d, with the equivariant lift supplied by the transport result. The main text does not separately specify the conjugation domain for this lifted torus use after the earlier Omega-restricted definition; retain that source issue rather than silently choosing a global or unit-cell conjugate. Dual optimality and appropriate periodicity of both corrections require the torus transport theorem.

comparisons.D26: Represent the full data by the finite dependent product indexed by the disjoint union Fin n and Fin m, assigning P to the first group and Q to the second. Coordinate projections then have the required marginals and independence, equivalently the joint law is P^n times Q^m. P and Q may differ and the sizes need not coincide. The assertion explicitly includes independence BETWEEN the two groups, in addition to independence within each group; it concerns random samples, not independent empirical measures as an unrelated added premise.

comparisons.D25: For the fixed known absolutely continuous P and the density-based target estimate Qhat_n from this section, require That_n measurable, map That_n P=Qhat_n and IsMinOn of T ↦ integral norm(x-T(x))^2 dP over the feasible transport class. comparisons.D8: Define varphi_star(y) by the source supremum over x in Omega of inner(x,y)-varphi(x), then minimize integral varphi dP + integral varphi_star dQ. Preserve the INFIMUM orientation and absence of a factor two in this semidual objective; the factor two occurs when converting to the quadratic-cost dual. Membership in L1(P) alone does not guarantee a finite conjugate, Q-integrability of it, or a pointwise representative independent of P-null modifications. Bochner integral returns zero on a nonintegrable input, so that fallback cannot silently define the intended optimization objective. Likewise a real supremum without boundedness can introduce a default. Record the source admissibility issue and prove the reparametrization equivalence only with the needed well-definedness conditions.

comparisons.D31: Retain the quantifier order: one epsilon0>0, then for every M,gamma>0 and 0<epsilon<epsilon0 a C>0 depending only on Omega,M,gamma,epsilon, uniformly over BOTH density choices in the specified positive Holder ball. The gradient of the potential pushes phat to qhat, and the potential is explicitly normalized to mean zero; the meaning of that mean must follow the source convention, not an arbitrary probability weighting. Its C2 norm is bounded by C, not just existence of two continuous derivatives. This is condition C2, not a theorem inferred from the compact convex smooth-boundary domain C1; the preceding discussion explicitly raises the uniform boundary regularity issue. Generic gradient/ContDiffOn supplies neither uniqueness, normalization nor a uniform bound.
